instruction: Parametric Straight-Run Staircase Read `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\params.json`; it contains: - `total_rise_m`: total vertical height of the staircase in meters - `total_run_m`: total horizontal length along the walking direction in meters - `max_rise_per_step_mm`: maximum allowed rise per step in millimeters - `tread_thickness_mm`: tread thickness in millimeters - `tread_width_m`: tread width in meters Compute `N = ceil(total_rise_m * 1000 / max_rise_per_step_mm)`, then compute `rise_per_step = total_rise_m / N` and `run_per_step = total_run_m / N`. Create a SketchUp model containing exactly `N` separate axis-aligned tread solids. For tread `i` (0-indexed), its bounding box must be exactly: X: [i * run_per_step, (i+1) * run_per_step] Y: [0, tread_width_m] Z: [(i+1) * rise_per_step - tread_thickness_mm/1000, (i+1) * rise_per_step] Do not include extra geometry. Save the native SketchUp model to `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\answer.skp`.
source: SketchUp Help (Push/Pull; Move and Copy); IRC R311.7 stair rise/run limits
